# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 25 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_025_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 5 — The Transition to the Shepherd

**1** The vision of the fifth kind which appeared to me, brothers and sisters, is as follows. **2** I was fasting and sitting on a certain mountain and giving thanks to the Lord for all the things which he had done for me, when I saw the Shepherd sitting beside me and saying: "Why have you come here early?" "Because, sir," I replied, "I keep a station here." **3** He said to me, "I am the angel of repentance. I have been sent to dwell with you for the remainder of your life." **4** It seemed to me that he had come to test me; I said to him: "Who are you? For I know to whom I have been entrusted and who it is who dwells with me." He said to me: "Do you not recognize me?" "No," I said. He said: "I am the Shepherd to whom you have been entrusted." **5** While he was speaking his form was changed, and I recognized him as the one to whom I had been entrusted. Immediately I was confounded, and fear seized me, and I was completely overwhelmed with grief because I had answered him so wickedly and foolishly. **6** He replied to me and said: "Do not be confounded; but be strong in my commandments which I am about to give you. For I have been sent," he said, "to show you again all the things which you saw before, and the most important things of all for your life. First of all, keep my commandments and you will be pleasing to God. **7** Write the Commandments and Parables." **8** When he had finished speaking with me he rose and went away. I did not see where he went. For there was a noise, and I turned and was afraid, thinking it was the beast. And when I looked, I saw nothing but the man sitting beside me.

---

*EMET note: Vision 5 = the transition. The "Shepherd" (poimen) = the angel of repentance (metanoias), who will deliver the Mandates and Similitudes. This chapter marks the structural pivot of the entire book. "Station" = an early Christian fasting practice.*
